splitBill.source: SECURITY_FIX_HANDOFF.md #20 - C is on the bill and claimed nothing; every line is RESOLVED, so her EVEN tip slice is real money and used to be computed then discarded

splitBill.name: discountExceedsSubtotal_clampedToTheItemsItRidesOn
splitBill.source: review/findings-domain.md D1 - a $30 voucher on $26 of food; the $9 tip keeps the bill total positive so the total check passes, and the sole claimant used to be handed a NEGATIVE tab that the `remaining > 0` filters then erased

splitBill.name: negativeLineTotal_costsZeroAndStaysExact
splitBill.source: review/findings-domain.md D4 - a negative line total makes largest-remainder leak a subunit and hands claimants negative shares; the app rejects it, the web guest path does not

splitBill.name: compedBill_evenTipStillSplitsAcrossParticipants
splitBill.source: review/findings-domain.md D2 - every line comped and claimed, so the bill IS finished; the even tip slices of the two who took nothing used to be computed and dropped

splitBill.name: compedBill_discountHasNothingToRideOn
splitBill.source: review/findings-domain.md D2 - the same comped bill with a discount; the `fullSubtotal <= 0` branch used to split a table-wide voucher among CLAIMANTS only, taking the one person who claimed below zero

splitBill.name: pricedZeroQuantityLine_isNotResolved
splitBill.source: review/findings-domain.md D5 - a priced line with no units is claimable by nobody, so $25 vanished from a bill the UI reported as finished (contrast zeroQuantityLine_resolvesAndChargesNobody, the zero-PRICED variant)

splitBill.name: portions_oddCentFollowsThePortionId_notRowOrder
splitBill.source: review/findings-domain.md D3 - three single-unit portions on a $10.00 line over 3 units; the rows arrive unordered, so whoever came first used to pay the 334. Recorded with the portions REVERSED, so the fix is what makes it pass.
